title: Hot Springs (Brahmakund), Rajgir - Sacred Waters of Healing and Devotion
content:
Hot Springs (Brahmakund), Rajgir

The Hot Springs of Rajgir, especially the famous Brahmakund, are among the most sacred and visited attractions in Bihar. Nestled at the foothills of the Vaibhava Hill, these natural thermal springs are known for their spiritual importance, healing properties, and connection to both Hindu and Buddhist traditions.

Historical and Religious Significance

The Brahmakund Hot Spring is believed to be 2,500 years old and holds immense importance in Hindu mythology. According to legends, Lord Brahma himself blessed these waters, making them sacred. The spring is located near the Saptaparni Caves, where the First Buddhist Council was held after Lord Buddha’s Mahaparinirvana.

The hot springs are also associated with Lord Buddha, who is said to have bathed here during his visits to Rajgir. This makes the site equally significant for both Hindu devotees and Buddhist pilgrims.

Spiritual and Medicinal Importance

The temperature of the Brahmakund water is around 45°C to 50°C and remains naturally warm throughout the year. It is rich in sulphur, believed to have therapeutic benefits for skin diseases, joint pain, and arthritis. Pilgrims bathe in the sacred tank with deep faith, believing it cleanses the body and soul.

Separate bathing areas are available for men and women, ensuring a peaceful and organized experience for visitors.

Nearby Attractions

  • Vishwa Shanti Stupa: The iconic white peace pagoda on Ratnagiri Hill, accessible by ropeway. Read more..
  • Venuvana Monastery: A serene bamboo grove where Lord Buddha meditated.
  • Griddhakuta Hill: The sacred site where Buddha delivered his teachings. Read more..
  • Ajatshatru Fort: A historic fort built by King Ajatshatru of Magadha.

Visitor Information

  • Location: At the base of Vaibhava Hill, Rajgir, Bihar
  • Timings: 6:00 AM - 6:00 PM
  • Entry Fee: Free
  • Best Time to Visit: October to March (pleasant weather for bathing and sightseeing)
  • Tip: Carry a towel and an extra set of clothes if you plan to take a bath in the spring.

faqs.question: Where are the Hot Springs located in Rajgir?
faqs.answer: The Hot Springs, including the famous Brahmakund, are located at the base of Vaibhava Hill in Rajgir, Bihar.

faqs.question: Why are the Rajgir Hot Springs famous?
faqs.answer: They are known for their spiritual significance and healing sulphur-rich waters, believed to cure skin and joint ailments.

faqs.question: What is the temperature of the water at Brahmakund?
faqs.answer: The water temperature remains around 45°C to 50°C throughout the year.

faqs.question: Are men and women allowed to bathe separately?
faqs.answer: Yes, there are separate bathing areas for men and women for convenience and privacy.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit the Hot Springs?
faqs.answer: The best time to visit is from October to March, when the weather is comfortable for bathing and sightseeing.
